before: password_hash creates a salted password hash using the selected algorithm; password_verify checks a candidate against the stored hash. The generated salt makes exact hash text nondeterministic, so tests should verify behavior rather than a fixed hash string.

PASSWORD_DEFAULT can evolve over PHP releases. Real storage must accommodate future hash lengths and a deliberate rehash policy; password_needs_rehash is an explicitly deferred production-authentication API reference, not a call required by this verification example. This synthetic fixture is not a complete login system: rate limiting, account isolation and transport security remain separate requirements.
Expected output or behavior: accepted. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

Optional local transfer task: Explain why comparing two newly generated salted hashes is the wrong password test. You may trace it without a PHP interpreter; reading completion is not proof of a local run.
